title: Win Your Race Goal: A Generalized Approach to Prediction of Running Performance
population: Complete running logs of 15 runners (15,686 runs) covering marathon to ultra distances, varied elevation gain, front-pack to back-of-pack
findings: An LSTM network with a regression approach reached 89.13% accuracy versus 85.21% for a time-series regression approach.
Over 60 races, accuracy was 90.4% for the LSTM, 80% for the Riegel formula and 87.5% for the UltraSignup formula.
The test set was the last 15 runs of each running log.
limitations: Only 15 runners; accuracy is not defined in the abstract; test runs are from the same athletes (not independent); single author, no external validation.
implications: Treat as hypothesis-generating; do not adopt an ML model on n = 15.
Back-test any ultra predictions against Riegel and an UltraSignup-style formula using per-athlete logged races.

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC re-fetched; numbers match. Accuracy metric undefined in the abstract.
